# Ezekiel 11 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Then the Spirit picked me up and carried me to the east gate of the LORD's Temple. There at the entrance were twenty-five men. Among them I recognized Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah — leaders of the people.

**2** The LORD said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who are plotting evil and giving wicked advice in this city.

**3** They say, 'Destruction isn't coming anytime soon. Let's build houses! This city is our cooking pot, and we are the choice meat inside — safe and protected.'"

**4** "Prophesy against them, son of man. Prophesy!"

**5** Then the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon me and told me to say: "This is what the LORD says: That is what you think, people of Israel. But I know every thought that runs through your minds.

**6** You have murdered many people in this city and filled its streets with the dead."

**7** So the Lord GOD says: "The victims you killed — they are the meat. The city is the pot. But you? I am going to drag you out of it.

**8** You were afraid of the sword, and the sword is exactly what I will bring against you, declares the Lord GOD.

**9** I will force you out of this city, hand you over to foreigners, and execute judgment on you.

**10** You will die by the sword. I will judge you at the borders of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

**11** This city will not be your safe cooking pot, and you will not be the protected meat inside it. I will judge you at the borders of Israel,

**12** and you will know that I am the LORD — whose laws you did not follow, whose rules you did not keep. Instead, you adopted the practices of the nations around you."

**13** While I was still prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah suddenly dropped dead. I fell facedown and cried out, "Lord GOD! Are You going to completely destroy what's left of Israel?"

**14** Then the LORD's message came to me:

**15** "Son of man, the people still living in Jerusalem have said about your fellow exiles — your own relatives, the whole house of Israel — 'They've been sent far from the LORD. This land belongs to us now.'

**16** So tell them this: The Lord GOD says: 'Yes, I sent them far away among the nations and scattered them across many countries. But I Myself have been a sanctuary for them — a little temple — wherever they've gone.'

**17** So tell them: The Lord GOD says: 'I will gather you from the nations. I will bring you back from the countries where you've been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel again.'

**18** When they return, they will remove every disgusting idol and detestable practice from the land.

**19** I will give them an undivided heart and put a new spirit in them. I will take out their stubborn heart of stone and give them a tender, responsive heart of flesh,

**20** so that they will follow My laws and carefully keep My commands. They will be My people, and I will be their God.

**21** But those whose hearts are still devoted to their vile idols and detestable practices — I will bring the consequences of their actions down on their own heads, declares the Lord GOD."

**22** Then the cherubim spread their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel hovered above them.

**23** And the glory of the LORD rose from over the city and stopped above the mountain east of it.

**24** Then the Spirit carried me back to Babylonia in the vision — back to the exiles. And the vision faded away.

**25** I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **11:3**: The leaders' arrogance is breathtaking — they think they're the choice meat, safely inside the pot. God flips it: the dead bodies in the streets are the meat. You? You're getting thrown OUT of the pot.

- **11:16**: Even in exile, God hasn't abandoned His people. He says, 'I've been a little sanctuary for you wherever you've gone.' God isn't stuck in a building. He travels with His people.

- **11:19-20**: This is one of the most hopeful promises in all of Scripture — God will perform heart surgery. He'll remove the stubborn, stony heart and replace it with one that actually wants to follow Him. This isn't willpower — it's transformation.

— PNEUMA
